The sheer carved cliff face above rises another five hundred feet of worked stone.

A desert mesa-castle occupies the entire flat summit of a sandstone pillar, its warm-ochre walls rising seamlessly from the natural rock so no join is visible. Crenellated ramparts ring the edge of the mesa, with ballista-platforms overhanging the sheer four-hundred-foot drop. The gatehouse is accessible only via a spiral ramp cut into the mesa exterior. At sunrise the entire fortress ignites in amber, copper and blood-orange light.

A Gothic dark-fortress perches atop a dead mountain leaking sickly green luminescence from rune-carved walls. Twisted spires spiral at unnatural angles, casting warped shadows. The curtain walls are studded with iron grotesques the size of wagons. A crumbling stone bridge leaps a thousand-foot void to reach the gatehouse, and the wind howling through the chasm below creates an unending, dirge-like moan audible for miles in every direction.

A mountain-cut cliff-fortress is hewn directly into a sheer granite ridge two thousand feet above the valley, its back wall the raw mountain itself. Tiered ramparts descend in steps, each defended by its own portcullis. The gatehouse opens from a narrow shelf of rock accessible only by a single carved staircase of one thousand steps hugging the cliff face. The banners visible from the valley floor are mere specks of color.

An elven tree-fortress spreads across seventeen ancient colossal oaks, their trunks wider than towers, woven together by graceful arching bridges of living branch and gilded wood. Platforms at ascending heights form three distinct defensive tiers, each ringed by archer galleries. The great hall occupies the merged canopy of the five central trees, its golden-leafed dome visible above the forest for a full day's ride in every direction.

A city-walled Minas-Tirith-coded fortress rises on a spur of white limestone in seven concentric tiers, each wall gleaming with embedded quartz veining that catches the sun and throws rainbow-scatter across the valley below. The outermost gate is wide enough to march an army through in column of twenty. The uppermost citadel tier holds a single great keep, its white tower reflecting light like a lighthouse beacon visible at sea.

A swamp drowned-castle rises half-submerged from a vast dark lake of still black water, its lower three tiers permanently flooded, archways opening directly onto the water. A flat-boat ferry is the only approach across a mile of open, motionless lake. The upper dry tiers are intact and occupied, their grey stone draped in hanging moss. The full silhouette reflected in the perfect-black water creates a ghostly mirror-castle below the real one.

An ice-fortress sits at the absolute spine of a mountain pass, its walls formed from compressed grey-blue ice blocks three meters thick, interlocked without mortar. Snow-drift ramparts rise along the battlements. The gatehouse is a tunnel of ice sixty feet deep, its walls carved with frost-rune reliefs that glow faintly blue in darkness. The approach is a road that crosses a open glacial field with no cover, brutally exposed to the wind.

A coastal island-fortress occupies a crescent-shaped sea-rock, its curtain walls following the exact curve of the natural island edge, presenting sheer castle wall to the ocean as though the island itself were a warship's hull. The inner harbor holds within the crescent's arm. Four round towers cap the seaward wall at equal intervals. The gatehouse faces the harbor. From a ship at sea, the entire structure resembles a breaking wave frozen in stone.

A desert sandstone fortress crowns a vast mesa above a canyon network, connected to the far rim by a single natural stone arch bridge that the builders have armored in fitted sandstone blocks. Warm-rose walls rise in three tiers. Ornate pierced-screen stonework decorates every parapet, casting geometric shadow patterns at noon. Wind-carved towers at each corner have been built upward from natural rock pinnacles, their irregular forms given purpose and height by clever masons.

A volcanic fire-castle clings to the outer slope of an active peak, its lower walls black with repeated lava-flow scorching and reinforced with iron-banded basalt. Channels have been deliberately cut to route lava-flows around the structure as a living moat. The central keep's crown is a cauldron-shaped platform where the volcanic glow backlights the entire silhouette against a permanent ash-purple sky, making the fortress appear to wear a halo of deep orange fire.

A Gothic necropolis-castle sprawls across a dead plateau, its cathedral-spired towers rising from a vast walled necropolis city of mausoleums and bone-inlaid chapel-halls. The outer walls run for a full mile, flanked by statue-rows of armored skeleton-knights carved in white marble. The central keep is a single spire of black granite eight hundred feet tall, its tip permanently wreathed in green mist. Every battlement surface is carved with screaming faces.

A dwarven hold-gate emerges from a valley-floor clifftop as a colossal tiered ziggurat of fitted granite, its faces carved with saga-reliefs ten meters tall depicting ancient battles. Each of the five ascending tiers has its own fighting platform and crenellated edge. The gate itself is a circular iron door sixty feet in diameter worked with a gear-driven opening mechanism of mithril teeth. Forge-smoke rises from every vent along the cliff-top ramparts.

A mountain cliff-fortress bridges a narrow mountain pass entirely, its curtain wall stretching cliff-to-cliff a full quarter-mile, with the single gatehouse arch as the only gap. The wall face rising from the pass floor is a sheer vertical hundred-foot drop of fitted stone. Behind the wall, the fortress stacks five more tiers up the mountainside, the rearmost a great keep whose rooftop is at the level of the neighboring peaks, surveying everything.

A city-walled harbor-fortress wraps an entire natural harbor in three rings of stone, the outermost ring standing in the sea itself on submerged foundations, its towers rising directly from the waves. The middle ring crowns the shore cliffs. The inner ring climbs the hill behind the city to the citadel summit. Chain-booms seal the harbor mouth between two heavy harbor-towers. The full silhouette from the sea resembles a stone crown laid atop a coastal hill.

An elven sky-citadel of white-and-silver architecture rests atop a waterfall-mountain, where three great cataracts plunge on either side of the cliff face that bears the fortress, framing the entire structure in perpetual cascading water and rainbow-mist. Slender spires rise above the falls' spray-cloud. The approach stair is cut directly behind one waterfall, forcing visitors to walk a stone corridor with the full force of the cataract thundering beyond a foot of carved rock.

A colossal Gothic spire-castle crowns a sheer obsidian cliff, its black-stone curtain walls descending in three stacked ramparts toward a chasm-bridge approach. Needle-thin towers pierce storm-lit clouds, each capped with iron crow-skull finials. The gatehouse yawns between two enormous carved-stone ravens, wings spread wide. Banners of midnight-purple snap in the gale. The central keep rises so high its summit vanishes into roiling thunderheads.

A Mediterranean cliff-fortress blazes white against a turquoise sea, its tiered limestone ramparts cascading down a sheer coastal headland in four successive curtain-wall rings. Golden-domed towers flank the grand gatehouse, their gilded surfaces catching noon sun like signal fires. Arched aqueducts bridge between tiers. The central palace-keep crowns the cliff-top, its carved-marble balustrades overlooking a two-hundred-foot vertical drop to wave-hammered rocks below.

A dwarven mountain-hold emerges from a granite massif, its gate-facade carved directly into a vertical mile of stone. Enormous rune-etched columns frame the entrance, flanked by terraced ramparts cut into the cliff-face at five ascending levels. Waterfalls pour between tiers, feeding a mist-shrouded moat. The inner citadel-towers, hewn from living rock, bristle above the ridgeline, their battlements glowing with forge-amber runes visible a league distant.

An elven sky-citadel rests on a cluster of three floating stone plateaus linked by arching root-and-crystal causeways. Slender silver towers spiral upward from each platform, wrapped in luminous white-blossomed vines. The central keep features a vast gilded canopy-dome supported by carved-tree pillars. Far below, a forest canopy stretches to the horizon, making the castle's elevation vertiginous. Dawn light refracts through crystalline spire-tips into cascading prismatic arcs across every courtyard.

A volcanic stronghold squats within a collapsed caldera, its basalt curtain walls hugging the inner crater rim. Rivers of slow lava trace channels between outer and inner ramparts, forming a natural moat of molten stone. Iron-chain drawbridges span the lava-flows. The central keep is a brutish obsidian tower-cluster, venting sulfur-smoke from forge-chimneys. Dragon-skull trophies mount every gatehouse parapet, and the entire fortress glows ember-orange against a soot-black sky.

A city-walled fortress rises in seven concentric tiers from a broad river-plain, each ring of white-stone walls higher than the last, topped with crenellated ramparts and banner-poles streaming gold and crimson. The gatehouse at each tier rivals a cathedral in scale. Spires cluster at the mountain-summit citadel above all rings, and a colossal king-statue flanks the grand entrance gate, its stone sword raised in permanent salute to all who approach across the vast open plain.

An ice citadel looms from a glacial shelf, carved directly from a continental ice-mass a thousand feet thick. Its curtain walls are translucent blue-white, revealing the frozen shapes of ancient siege-engines within the ice. Blizzard-swept ramparts cascade down in four jagged tiers. Pale-bone towers rise from each corner, their battlements rimmed with hanging icicle-spires. The gatehouse arch is formed by two glacial dragon-skulls, and the central keep catches winter light like an enormous frozen lantern.

A coastal sea-keep dominates an island of sheer black basalt, its curtain walls rising directly from the churning surf. The approach is a wind-lashed stone causeway barely wide enough for two horses, flanked by crashing Atlantic-scale waves. Four drum-towers anchored at cliff-corners support a web of connecting wall-walks. The central keep is a brutish drum of storm-grey stone, topped with a signal-pyre platform. Crossed-chain boom-anchors guard the sea-gate below the waterline.

A swamp tor-castle perches atop a lone limestone pillar rising from an endless fog-shrouded marshland, its curtain walls gripping the rock's edge with iron clamps and buttressed arches. A single rope-and-plank bridge connects it to solid ground a terrifying distance away. The multi-tiered ramparts are crusted with moss and ancient barnacles. Twisted iron towers rise from each corner, hung with lanterns that cast diseased-green reflections onto the black water far below.

A desert mesa-castle crowns a sandstone plateau, its honey-amber walls blending with the rock until the eye resolves battlements, towers, and arched gateways from the stone itself. Three tiers of curtain walls descend the mesa's stepped sides, each connected by ramp-roads carved into the cliff-face. The central keep features an enormous open-air solar-tower with a gilded sunburst capstone that blazes like a second sun at dawn. Red-ochre banners stream from every tower-top across a boundless sea of dunes.

A mountain-cut fortress seals an entire alpine pass, its curtain walls stretching cliff-to-cliff across the gorge, rising eighty feet of dressed granite with no gap for wind or army. The gatehouse-tower erupts from the wall's center, bristling with bolt-thrower platforms at every level. Behind the wall, the inner keep is built into the mountain's own flank, its upper halls emerging as stone towers from the rock-face. The approach is a bare, exposed road visible for three miles.

A Gothic necropolis-castle occupies an entire dead-city plateau, its cathedral-spires and ossuary-towers rising in a jagged skyline of carved-bone buttresses and gargoyle-encrusted curtain walls. The gatehouse is flanked by colossal kneeling-skeleton statuary, each the height of a tower. Multiple wards descend the plateau in rings, every wall topped with iron-spike palisades. The central keep-cathedral fuses throne-room and reliquary, its spire a single obsidian needle piercing a perpetual eclipse-halo cloud.

A dwarven underground-city gate faces a mountain valley, its entrance facade a sheer-carved cliff of dark granite rising three hundred feet, framed by eight sequential archways of diminishing size that draw the eye into profound depth. Six tiers of fortified balconies line each side of the entrance-cut, connected by stone staircases and iron-railed platforms. The outer gatehouse is a full fortress in itself, separated from the main facade by a deep ravine crossed by a single arched bridge.

An elven forest-citadel weaves through and above an ancient canopy of silver-barked trees, its living-wood towers grown upward and shaped by centuries of patient craft into spiraling forms. Three concentric rings of treebound walls define its wards, linked by root-arched gatehouses. Starlight-reflective ponds fill the courtyard basins between tiers. The central spire is the tallest living tree on the continent, shaped into a king's hall, its crown a thousand feet above the forest floor.

A storm-king's Gothic castle clings to a coastal headland beaten by permanent tempest, its dark-slate ramparts buttressed with flying arches against the perpetual gale-force winds. The outer curtain wall is broad enough to race horses across its top. Chain-lightning rods cap every spire, each tower festooned with iron-link pennants that sing a constant metallic chord. The approach is a crumbling cliff road with sheer sea-drops on both sides, half-eaten by centuries of storm erosion.

A city-fortress of layered concentric rings fills an enormous river-island, every ring's wall taller and older than the one outside it, giving the whole a geological strata appearance. The outermost ring is a working harbor-wall with sea-gates of wrought iron. Each successive inner ring is more fortified and more ornate, culminating in a central citadel-palace of white-and-gold marble with soaring spires. Thousands of pennants and flying buttresses give the skyline an impossibly complex silhouette against the sunset.

A floating-stone sky-fortress drifts above a permanent cloudbank, its foundations a cluster of inverted stone pyramids that project downward into the cloud-layer while the castle structure rises above. Enormous anchor-chains tether it to mountain-peaks below, clanking in the updrafts. The fortress has four ascending rampart-rings, the topmost open to open sky. The approach is a winch-lifted drawbridge-ramp from a clifftop staging-point, swaying sickeningly over a cloud-filled void of indeterminate depth.

An ice-encased winter fortress crowns a frozen tundra ridge, its square Norman-style curtain walls encased in centuries of accumulated glacial growth until the entire castle is a hybrid of stone and ice, rampart-tops bristling with natural ice-spikes that rival the tower heights. The gatehouse is a tunnel carved through a solid ice-accretion thirty feet thick. Rune-carved standing stones flank the outer approach, each one slowly being swallowed by the advancing ice-sheet over the millennia.

A volcanic fire-castle spans a lava-lake island, connected to the crater rim by three black-iron chain-link bridges wide enough for siege-engines. Its curtain walls glow with heat-crack fissures filled with smoldering orange light. The gatehouse towers are sheathed in fire-blackened dragon-scale plate bolted directly to the stone. The central keep-tower is a chimney-castle, its hollow core a permanent up-draft of super-heated air. Molten channels run through open aqueducts between each rampart ring.

A Highlands Gothic fortress occupies a glacial lake island, accessible only by narrow boat across fog-heavy dark water a mile from shore. Its curtain walls rise sheer from the waterline with no beach or landing-stage, just iron ladder-rungs set into the submerged stone. Three rings of walls rise in terraced rings toward the summit keep, its towers capped with slate-grey spires. Enormous carved-stag heads flank the water-gate, and heraldic banners hang limp in the permanent lake-mist.
